- No text, letters, numbers or logos (slots as empty rects); no images, filters or masks; up to 120 KB per prop.

STYLE: 2.5D LIT LAYERS (for cinematic moments, mood, emphasis: the camera pushes through depth and the light can change)
- A layout painter's room in vector layers: accurate two-point perspective, a clear value plan (light, middle, dark masses) before colour, and depth that the parallax camera can travel through.
- Every depth layer (far, mid, near) is split so the engine can relight it: the base shapes in local colour (outside the classed groups, as the contract says), then <g class="lm-shadow"> form and cast shadows, <g class="lm-light"> key-light shapes, <g class="lm-hi"> thin bright rim edges on silhouettes against the window, <g class="lm-atmos"> haze and light shafts.
- Materials read through light, not line: no outlines; edges come from value change. Glass reflects the window as one or two pale shapes; a satin floor shows a faint sheen under the window light, as a lighter low-opacity shape.
- Light setups are sibling groups inside each depth layer, each holding its own lm-shadow, lm-light, lm-hi and lm-atmos groups: id="setup_day" first (the main delivery: the scene's light). After I approve it, add id="setup_evening" (low sun, long shadows, lamps on) and id="setup_night" (window dark, lamps and screens are the lights) in the same file. The base shapes are shared. In this style a variant that only changes the light (evening, night) IS a setup, not a separate file; a variant that moves objects is a separate file.
- Paint what is behind every object: the wall and floor continue complete under the furniture of the mid and near layers, so a parallax move never shows a hole; the far layer runs past the frame into the overscan.
- Light: One warm key with believable cast shadows (window panes projected on the floor and table, stretched by perspective), a cool fill from the opposite side, light shafts as long transparent polygons in lm-atmos (2-stop linear gradients allowed there, light to transparent). Shadows are cool and coloured, never grey.
- Texture: Very little: a soft gradient across large walls in lm-atmos only. No noise.
- Depth: Aerial perspective: the far layer is lighter, cooler and lower in contrast, with haze over it at the amount the scene's Light paragraph states (0.3 to 0.45 for a deep space when it states none); the near layer is darkest and may be partly silhouetted against the light.
- Quality bar: A feature-animation colour key translated into clean vector layers: the light tells you the time of day and the mood before anything moves.

THE WORLD: METAPHOR WORLDS
A fictional fishing harbour town of about 600 people on a granite headland on a cold North Atlantic coast, in late May, when icebergs drift south past the coast. The town sits around a small sheltered harbour that opens to the east; a white lighthouse stands on the headland south of the harbour mouth, with its keeper's house and a walled kitchen garden in the lee of the tower; behind the town a footpath climbs a bare hill to a summit cairn; across the narrow inlet north of the town a new concrete road bridge is being built from both banks. Every set is a spot in this one place, so the same lighthouse, the same granite and the same sea recur. No real town is drawn.

- two-storey timber houses with steep gable roofs and narrow clapboard siding, painted in a few muted colours (ochre, oxblood red, slate blue, off-white) with white window trims and six-pane sash windows, standing on low granite footings and stepping up the slope; no shop signs or names
- the harbour: a straight quay of squared granite blocks with a concrete capping, black cast-iron bollards about 5 m apart and 0.5 m back from the edge, vertical timber fenders on the quay face, a steel ladder recessed into the wall; a curved rubble breakwater of big granite blocks across the south side of the harbour mouth, with a short white light tower with a red lantern on its head, and a small green light on a white post at the quay's end
- single-storey fishing stores along the quay: timber sheds with pitched roofs of dark grey corrugated sheet, wide double doors, weathered silver-grey boards
- the lighthouse: a round tapering tower of white-painted masonry about 18 m tall on the headland's highest rock, a black-painted iron gallery with railings, a glazed lantern with diagonal glazing bars and a red-painted domed roof with a ball vent; inside, below the lantern, a round watch room holds the weight-driven clockwork that still turns the lens; the station is kept as a working heritage light, wound by hand by a part-time keeper
- the land: bare grey-pink granite in rounded outcrops and cliffs, low wind-shaped spruce in the hollows, crowberry and grass heath, small dark ponds; no tall trees
- the new bridge: a concrete box-girder road bridge built by the balanced cantilever method, two slim piers in the inlet, each carrying a deck that grows outward both ways in 5 m segments, with yellow form travellers at the tips of the growing deck and a tower crane beside each pier
Materials: grey-pink granite, painted clapboard (muted ochre, oxblood, slate blue, off-white), silver-grey weathered timber, black cast iron and painted steel, white-painted masonry, fresh pale-grey concrete, rope and netting, a deep blue-green sea and white-and-pale-blue ice; signal red and orange only on things that carry them in life (the lantern roof, the breakwater light, lifebuoys, fishing floats, a rescue boat's collar), and warning yellow only on the bridge's construction plant (the cranes, the form travellers).
